correctness.rationale: For all n≥2 and integer d,m, represent a²+b²−dc²=m on ordered unit triples. For odd p the known exact binary square count B_p(t) is p−eps for nonzero t and p+(p−1)eps for t=0, where eps=chi_p(−1). Summing over c yields unrestricted ternary p²+p*chi_p(d)*chi_p(m) when p∤d; inclusion–exclusion over a=0,b=0,c=0 enforces all units and gives four F_p cases, with p|d separately factoring p−1. For every odd p-adic lifting step, ∂/∂b=2b unit gives exactly p² lifts per old solution for a specified target. Odd squares fill exactly the 1(mod2^min(e,3)) coset uniformly, giving F_(2^e) and its support; CRT factors arbitrary modulus and permits independent minimization of local targets. Comparison of z∈{0,±1} produces piecewise minima, including exceptional p3,5. Independently directly enumerated ordered unit triples for every residue d,m at p=3,5,7,11,13,17,19 and matched every fiber and sharp local minimum. Infinite-modulus theorem rests on explicit character sums, Hensel lifting and CRT, not finite tests.

value.rationale: Existing work characterizes when all residue targets are representable by a²+b²−dc² with unit variables. Complete target-fiber multiplicities, dyadic zero/nonzero support and sharp worst-target counts are natural quantitative refinements needed for constrained quadratic-form local densities. The theorem preserves d divisible by p, p=2 and exceptional small primes, making it more useful than a routine rephrasing of the existential criterion.

limitations: Only exact ordered triples of units; d and m can be divisible by modulus primes; dyadic congruence conditions handled separately.
Elementary character-sum method is prior known; only full fiber/worst-target synthesis assessed as potentially novel.
